findings.reason: the loader's declared boundary source must name both arcs (or state that `surfABVxp` alone closes the contour), or the §7 builder receives half a boundary and the reference geometry is wrong away from the top of the plasma.
findings.text: the changed text names `surfABVxp` as "the last closed surface", but the plan's own PSRC inventory records the boundary as two complementary arcs — `surfABVxp` (604x11520, above the X-point) and `surfBLWxp` (204x11520, below the X-point) (docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-machine-map/jtmm-psrc-selene-inventory.html:44-45) — and `resample_lcfs_radii` (imas_ambix/worldmodel/equilibrium_labels.py:363-372) ray-casts a contour that must span the full [0,2pi) about the axis, so the above-X-point arc alone is an open contour and its upper rays would be read as NaN

response_events.reason: surfABVxp is not an open arc. imas-efit's scripts/build_selene_validation_ids.py decodes each row ([3, nA, R[300], 3, nA, Z[300]], R and Z in mm) to a contour that is already closed, first point equal to last at the X-point, and writes it as the whole last closed surface in boundary.outline. surfBLWxp traces the divertor legs beyond the X-point and is excluded from the LCFS on purpose. The SELENE loader node will assert that closure (first point equals last) in its test when it is scoped.
